items.statement: Over 12 weeks, fewer than 60 percent of eligible patient-shifts on the ward will have a screen that was performed, with completion on night shifts at least 20 percentage points below day shifts.
items.rationale: Need is high because the ward must choose where to intervene; novelty is low because the pattern is known elsewhere; feasibility is high because the research nurse and approvals are in place.
items.risks: Observer effect on sampled shifts; low occupancy weeks.

items.statement: Patients with dementia will be screened on at least 15 percentage points fewer shifts than patients without dementia.
items.rationale: The highest-risk group is screened least elsewhere (claim c3).

items.statement: Fewer than half of positive screens will be followed by a medical review within 24 hours.
items.rationale: Screening only helps if positive results are acted on (claim c4).
items.risks: Few positive screens in a 12-week window.

summary: Three descriptive hypotheses; h1 selected as the main estimate, h2 and h3 as pre-specified secondary estimates.
